stories.headline: YouTuber Hank Green says his AI usage is ‘not healthy’
facts: Title: YouTuber Hank Green says his AI usage is ‘not healthy’
Hank Green, a novelist, comedian, and [YouTuber with 3.2 million subscribers](https://www.youtube.com/@hankschannel), recently apologized to his audience for his growing reliance on AI chatbots.

The [controversy](https://kotaku.com/famous-science-youtuber-admits-he-has-unhealthy-relationship-with-ai-after-facing-backlash-over-recent-video-2000720908) started when, in the middle of [a video posted on the educational channel Complexly](https://youtu.be/C5bwAv9Xdz8?si=aatwfElDa4D2UieM), Green incongruously used the phrase “I appreciate the pushback,” l

In a since-deleted post on X, Green acknowledged that he’d produced the video “under a ton of pressure” and used ChatGPT “for research on this script.” At the same time, he said the “pushback” line was actually a response to the episode’s guest.

Green then [offered a more in-depth apology](https://www.reddit.com/r/nerdfighters/comments/1vbmoj5/comment/p0vzmog/) on Reddit, where he said he was “mortified” that he’d “let so many people down” and that he plans to reduce his video production as a result.

stories.headline: This $9 key physically locks your most addictive apps
facts: Title: This $9 key physically locks your most addictive apps

Screen-time apps aren’t effective for many people because, in the end, they depend on your willpower. They remind you to stop scrolling or let you set timers, but such notifications can be easy to ignore.

[Autonomous Key](https://www.autonomous.ai/key) takes a different approach to this issue simply by being a physical device. It’s an NFC key that pairs with a companion app to let you lock away distracting apps. So instead of tapping a button to bypass the block, you have to physically scan the key with your phone to regain access to your locked apps. Each un

That physical requirement is what makes the idea compelling. Instead of depending on your self-control, you can leave the NFC key in another room, or even at the office or gym, turning a mindless impulse to open Instagram or TikTok into a deliberate decision that requires extra effort.
At just $9, Autonomous Key is considerably cheaper than its competitors like Blok ($29), Unpluq ($26.50), and Brick ($59).

stories.headline: Sam Altman is still making the case for parenting via ChatGPT
facts: Title: Sam Altman is still making the case for parenting via ChatGPT

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman seemed excited to share what he called a “cool use case” on Friday, [posting](https://x.com/sama/status/2083221585792762171) that parents could “connect your family calendars and explain your kids’ interests” to [the company’s new product ChatGPT Work](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/09/openai-launches-its-new-family-of-models-with-gpt-5

Altman’s post prompted lots of virtual eye-rolling, including [a simple response](https://x.com/_AlexHirsch/status/2083268104742924484) from Alex Hirsch, creator of the animated series “Gravity Falls”: “What if you just talked to your children”?

Hirsch’s question seems to have gone even more viral than Altman’s initial post — while Altman’s comment has been reposted around 300 times and liked around 9,600 times (as of Saturday morning), Hirsch’s response has been reposted 9,000 times and received 122,000 likes.

This isn’t the first time a tech CEO has promised that AI can shield users — and specifically users’ morning commutes — from the messiness and inefficiency of human experience. Last year, [Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said he’d stopped listening his favorite podcasts](https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/17/microsofts-satya-nadella-is-choosing-chatbots-over-podcast
